title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool and parallel calls with result injection and retry policies
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: developer ergonomics for tool/function calling have been a recurring friction point: multi-tool workflows require either serial orchestration (slow) or ad-hoc parallelism in user code (error-prone). This PR introduces a first-class execution ergonomics layer that supports: coordinated parallel tool invocation with configurable concurrency, deterministic injection points for tool results into the model context/stream, per-tool retry/backoff policies, at-most-once vs at-least-once invocation semantics, and improved streaming stability for tool output. Changes touch the runtime orchestration loop, the OpenAI-compat function_call surface, and SDK helpers so callers can request: (1) tools:[] parallel=true concurrency=3; (2) tool_result_injection: after_model_message | before_next_chunk; and (3) retry_policy: none | idempotent | best_effort. Implementation notes: a short-lived concurrency pool lives in the request execution context and is bounded by tenant-level config; tool outputs are captured as structured fragments (type=tool_output) and injected into the streaming path so clients can observe interleaved model tokens and tool results; retries are performed per-tool with jittered exponential backoff respecting a configurable max_attempts and idempotency hints; the OpenAI-compat layer accepts multiple function calls and maps them to the new orchestration API, emitting function_call metadata in the stream for incremental client consumption. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves existing single-tool, serial semantics unless the new flags are set. Testing: unit tests for orchestration, fakes for parallel tool endpoints, e2e against the openai-compat harness, perf microbenchmarks showing median latency improvements for multi-tool requests compared to serial baseline. This PR also adds docs and an SDK example in the python SDK. Linked linear items and support ticket included for customer migration guidance.
commit_summary: feat(runtime): introduce parallel tool orchestration loop with configurable concurrency and cancellation
feat(api): extend OpenAI-compat function_call surface to accept multiple tools and execution flags
feat(streaming): inject tool_result events into token stream (type=tool_output) and stabilize interleaving semantics
feat(sdk-python): add high-level helper ToolRunner and example for parallel tool calls
test: add unit/integration tests and perf harness for multi-tool scenarios
docs: add API docs, migration guide, and example snippets
changed_files: redwood-helm-charts/values.yaml (tweak default concurrency limit for demo)
review_comments: Liam Chen: Are we confident the concurrency pool won't blow up memory for large tenant counts? Suggest we gate max concurrency by both per-tenant config and global server-side limit.
Asha Patel (author): Added a global hard cap and an admission check that rejects requests exceeding tenant quota. Updated execution_context.go to reserve token/buffer budgets per task.
Marisol Ortega: Please add more detail in docs about semantics of at-most-once vs at-least-once and how retries affect model traces. Also request an example for common idempotent tools.
Asha Patel: Added migration doc and python example demonstrating idempotent retry_policy usage with an external cache key. Clarified semantics in tool-calling.md.
David Nguyen: Integration tests flaky on first run due to ordering of stream events; can we make emitter deterministic for tests?
Asha Patel: Introduced deterministic timestamps/ordering hooks under REDWOOD_TEST_DETERMINISTIC to stabilize tests. Re-ran CI.
Liam Chen: Approving with small nits (naming of ToolResult vs ToolOutput).
Marisol Ortega: LGTM — docs reviewed and example is clear.
ci_checks: integration-tests: initial failure on stream-ordering flaky test, rerun passed (420s)
perf-microbenchmarks: median latency improvement 28% vs serial baseline (see artifacts)
release_notes: Add support for parallel tool/function calls, tool result streaming/injection, and per-tool retry policies. Default behavior unchanged. New SDK helpers and docs included. See migration guide for switching to parallel invocation and for retry policy recommendations.
additional_context: Perf: bench harness shows improved median latency when invoking 3 external tools in parallel vs serial baseline; peak memory overhead measured and constrained via admission checks.
Security: tool outputs are treated as untrusted; runtime enforces sanitization hooks before injecting into model context. KMS flags unaffected.
Backcompat: OpenAI-compat layer defaults preserve single-tool behavior unless tools[]+parallel flags are used. Clients upgrading are opt-in.
